newsitem.title: USA: U.S. junk corp primary market off to strong start. [CORRECTED 18:30 GMT]
newsitem.headline: U.S. junk corp primary market off to strong start. [CORRECTED 18:30 GMT]

text.p: The primary market for corporate junk bonds in the U.S. got off to a strong start as Colt Telecommunications Group, a U.K.-based local telephone service provider, priced a blowout $175 million 12 percent zero coupon bond deal on Monday, sources said.

Investor demand for zero coupon paper from start-up high-tech companies has been weak recently, but the Colt transaction, lead managed by Morgan Stanley & Co Inc, was extremely well received, junk players said.
The 10-year zero offering was increased to $175 million from $150 million and priced on the inside of price talk.
Sources say the main reason behind the strong demand was that investors were optimistic about Colt's strategy to offer low-cost local telephone service in the European market.

Scholastic Brands Inc has sold $90 million in senior subordinated notes to yield 11 percent via Lehman Brothers Inc on Tuesday morning, sources say. That deal was also priced on the low end of price talk which was 11 to 11-1/4 percent. The notes were rated B3/B-minus.
The new issue market for junk bonds is expected to be quite busy this week as issuers rush to price well over $1 billion in new deals before the holidays.
The new issue market of investment-grade debt is also off to a strong start this week, syndicate officials said.
Philip Morris Co plans to sell $500 million in a2/A-rated notes due 2003 on Tuesday via a Goldman Sachs & Co-led syndicate, sources said.

Deutsche Bank plans to tap the market on Tuesday with a $1.0 billion (corrects amount of deal from $1.2 billion) Aa1/AA-plus rated 10-year yankee deal via lead manager Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, sources say.
Nike Inc is also readying a $150 million seven-year debt offering via lead manager Goldman Sachs which is expected to price this week.
Earlier this morning, Consolidated Natural Gas Co sold $150 million in A1/AA-minus 6-5/8 percent notes due 2008 via Chase Securities. Chase won the right to underwrite the deal via a competitive bid.
